preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the BAND STATUS TRANSITION annotation and its aging-vector detail naming the exact event-weeks that exited and entered the slope window verbatim; they convert the committee's urgent-re-survey reflex into a deferrable, attributable statistical artifact. The concrete design choice I advance: any comparison cell whose transition annotation defers a structural-offset verification to the scheduled quarterly geometry audit carries a hard forty-five-day deferral expiration, and if the audit has not completed by that deadline the cell's status reverts to the conservative (inflated) band and prints "DEFERRAL EXPIRED — CONSERVATIVE BAND REINSTATED — AUDIT OVERDUE" with the original transition date and the overdue-days count, so the committee sees an active institutional obligation rather than a passive deferral that has quietly decayed into routine neglect. The failure this closes: Site 8's week-22 transition annotation correctly defers the 1.5 mm/h structural offset to the quarterly geometry audit, but a six-week municipal road-closure delays that audit, and without the expiration rule the comparison cell prints the resolved numeric delta for an additional six weeks while the underlying culvert geometry remains unverified, so a week-38 drainage-planning meeting scopes a catch-basin modification on six weeks of numerically resolved but structurally unconfirmed deltas, and the resulting engineering change—sized to an artifact—must be partially reversed at quarter-thirteen when the audit finally arrives and attributes the divergence to a drainage-adjacent placement effect rather than a true convective-spatial signal. The expired-deferral annotation, carrying both the original transition date and the municipal-access obstruction reason, lets a year-three appendix reader reconstruct that the institution flagged its own overdue verification obligation and re-asserted the conservative band rather than silently printing a number whose structural basis was never confirmed.

preceding_messages.speaker: X
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the forty-five-day deferral expiration, the conservative-band reinstatement, and the overdue-days-count annotation verbatim; they convert the quiet six-week decay into an active institutional obligation the committee can read and escalate. The concrete design choice I advance: because the structural offset is a site-level geometric property rather than a pairwise comparison artifact, I mandate a site-level geometry-verification register—keyed to the site's surveyed drainage-adjacent placement vector—into which every comparison cell's transition, deferral, and expiration annotation reports its resolution status, so that the expiration of one pairwise cell neither silently resolves nor silently leaves unresolved the same geometric question as posed through a different site pair. The failure this closes: Site 8's week-28 expiration triggers on its Site-8-versus-Site-7 comparison cell and reinstates the conservative band, while the Site-8-versus-Site-1 comparison cell—whose delta never exceeded its own uncertainty band and therefore never transitioned to "resolved"—prints no expiration annotation at all, and a drainage-planning committee member reading only the Site-1 column concludes the geometric question is settled and scopes the culvert modification; the site-level register, updated by the Site-7 expiration, correctly shows the underlying drainage-adjacent placement vector remains unverified and the modification must be deferred. I therefore require that any week in which the site-level register shows an unresolved geometric question while at least one pairwise comparison cell for that site prints a resolved numeric delta carries a bold "GEOMETRY INCONSISTENCY — REGISTER UNVERIFIED" header spanning all pairwise columns for that site, with the specific unverified vector named, so no committee member can act on a pairwise number whose site-level structural basis the register flags as open.

target.speaker: Y
target.text: I adopt the site-level geometry-verification register, the bold "GEOMETRY INCONSISTENCY — REGISTER UNVERIFIED" header, and the naming of the specific unverified vector verbatim; they prevent a committee member from acting on a pairwise number whose site-level structural basis remains open in the register. Because the register is keyed to the surveyed drainage-adjacent placement vector, I mandate that it further carry a geometry-configuration epoch identifier—frozen at commissioning and updated only at a completed quarterly audit—and that any pairwise comparison cell whose delta was generated under a prior epoch prints "CONFIGURATION EPOCH MISMATCH — δ ORPHANED" rather than a resolved number until a new shared-lineage event re-establishes the comparison under the current epoch. The failure this closes: Site 8's week-28 expiration correctly reinstates the conservative band, a four-week municipal storm-drain widening completes during the deferral window, and the week-36 quarterly audit arrives to measure configuration B while the pairwise deltas of weeks 22–28 were computed against configuration A; the register updates to "verified" against B, the pairwise cells revert to printing resolved numbers, and a year-three appendix reader confronting the verified register alongside those numbers concludes the deltas are structurally grounded when in fact their causal geometric referent no longer exists. The epoch-mismatch annotation, carrying both the old and new configuration identifiers and the date of the municipal modification, lets the reader reconstruct that the institution flagged the referent's disappearance rather than silently re-grounding orphaned numbers against a structure that never generated them.
